dedupe_keys.name: national population database npd great britain

description: The National Population Database (NPD) is a point-based GIS dataset that combines building locations from providers such as Ordnance Survey with population information for those locations, mostly from government statistics, allowing detailed local analysis anywhere in Great Britain. It was created by the Health and Safety Executive with Staffordshire University in 2004 and is maintained by HSE; the data.gov.uk entry was last modified on 19 June 2026. It helps assess the societal risk of major hazard sites such as oil refineries, chemical works and gas holders, and includes sensitive populations such as schools and hospitals whose occupants may be more vulnerable and harder to evacuate. Data are grouped in five themes: residential, sensitive populations, transport, workplaces and leisure. Coverage is Great Britain. Access: the NPD portal on ArcGIS Hub, with further HSE data products described on HSE's site. Licence: a Creative Commons Attribution licence is given on the data.gov.uk entry; portal terms were not read today. Free. Caveats: population values are modelled from statistics; access conditions for the full data may differ from the portal overview. Simulation uses: building-level population exposure for industrial accident, flood and emergency evacuation models. Related records: the Harris County building population estimates.
